According to the shrine's legend, there was originally one enshrined deity, Tenho Nichimiko, but later Nomi no Sukune and Sugawara Michizane were enshrined, making the number three.

=== About the enshrined deity ===The main enshrined deity, {{ill|Ame no Hohi|bg|Аме Но Хохи|fa|آمه-نو-هوهی|fr|Ame no Hohi|it|Ame no Hohi|ja|アメノホヒ|pl|Niebiański Duch Przewodni|ru|Амэ но Хохи|simple|Ame no Hohi|zh|天菩比神|qid=Q10940685|lt=Amenohohi}}, is described in ``{{ill|Nihon Shoki|ar|نيهون شوكي|as|নিহন শ্ব'কি|az|Nihon şoki|bcl|Nihon Shoki|bg|Нихоншоки|ca|Nihon Shoki|cs|Nihonšoki|de|Nihonshoki|el|Νιχόν Σόκι|eo|Nihon Ŝoki|es|Nihonshoki|eu|Nihon Shoki|fa|نیهون شوکی|fi|Nihonshoki|fr|Nihon shoki|gl|Nihon Shoki|he|ניהון שוקי|hi|निहोन शोकी|hr|Nihon Shoki|hu|Nihonsoki|id|Nihon Shoki|it|Nihon shoki|ja|日本書紀|jv|Nihon Shoki|ko|일본서기|la|Nihon Shoki|mk|Нихон шоки|ms|Nihon Shoki|my|နိဟွန်းရှောခိ|nl|Nihon Shoki|no|Nihonshoki|oc|Nihon shoki|pl|Nihon-shoki|pt|Nihon Shoki|rsk|Нихон Шоки|ru|Нихон сёки|sco|Nihon Shoki|sh|Nihon Shoki|simple|Nihon Shoki|sl|Nihon Šoki|sq|Nihon Shoki|sr|Нихон шоки|sv|Nihonshoki|ta|நிஹான் ஷோகி|th|นิฮงโชกิ|tl|Nihon Shoki|tr|Nihon Shoki|uk|Ніхон Сьокі|uz|Nihon shoki|vi|Nhật Bản thư kỷ|zh|日本書紀|zh_min_nan|Ji̍t-pún Su-kì|zh_yue|日本書紀|qid=Q813935}}'' as ``Kore Izumo. As you can see, he became the ancestor god of the ancient clan '''{{ill|Haji clan|ja|土師氏|zh|土師氏|qid=Q10927758}}'' (Hajiuji, Hajiren and later Haji Sukune). The Haji clan is the {{ill|Tomonomiyatsuko|ja|伴造|zh|伴造|qid=Q11381545}} clan of Hajibu, which is responsible for the production of {{ill|Haniwa|ar|هانيوا|ca|Haniwa|cs|Haniwa|de|Haniwa|eo|Haniva|es|Haniwa|fi|Haniwa|fr|Haniwa|hu|Haniva|id|Haniwa|it|Haniwa|ja|埴輪|mk|Ханива|nl|Haniwa|pl|Haniwa|pt|Haniwa|ru|Ханива|sr|Ханива|sv|Haniwa|th|ฮานิวะ|tr|Haniwa|uk|Ханіва|zh|埴轮|qid=Q849376}}, {{ill|Earthenware|af|Erdeware|ar|فخاريات|bn|মৃৎপাত্র|ca|Pisa (ceràmica)|cs|Pórovina|da|Lertøj|de|Irdengut|dga|Laa Meɛraa|es|Loza|eu|Loza (materiala)|fa|سفال|fr|Terracotta (matériau)|frr|Pottjüch|gl|Louza|he|חרס|hu|Cserép|id|Tembikar tanah liat|it|Terracotta|ja|土器|ko|토기|li|Steigood|nds_nl|Diggelwark|nl|Aardewerk|no|Leirtøy|pnb|مٹی دے برتݨ|simple|Earthenware|sv|Lergods|ta|மண் பானை|th|เครื่องดินเผาเนื้อพรุน|tr|Toprak eşya|uk|Глиняний посуд|vi|Đồ đất nung|zh|土器|qid=Q1377111}}, funerals, and {{ill|mausoleum|ja|陵墓|ko|능묘|qid=Q65292090}} {{Sfn| The Haji clan (ancient clan) |2010}}, the distant ancestor of the Haji clan, {{ill|Nomi no Sukune|de|Nomi-no-Sukune|fa|نومی نو سوکونه|ff|Nomi no Sukune|fr|Nomi-no-Sukune|ja|野見宿禰|ru|Номи-но Сукунэ|uk|Номі-но-Сукуне|zh|野見宿禰|qid=Q965742}}, is also the person whose Haniwa tradition is recorded in the Nihon Shoki. This Haji clan has four limbs, which appear as "four bells," in an article dated December 30, 9th year of {{ill|Enryaku|de|Enryaku|es|Enryaku|fa|انریاکو|fr|Ère Enryaku|ia|Enryaku|id|Enryaku|it|Enryaku|ja|延暦|ko|엔랴쿠|pt|Enryaku|ru|Энряку (нэнго)|simple|Enryaku|sr|Енрјаку|tr|Enryaku|uk|Енряку (ненґо)|zh|延曆|zh_yue|延曆|qid=Q1373176}} ({{ill|790|ab|790|af|790|am|790 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|790|ar|790|ary|790|ast|790|avk|790|az|790|azb|۷۹۰ (میلادی)|ban|790|bcl|790|be|790|be_x_old|790|bg|790|bn|৭৯০|bpy|মারি ৭৯০|br|790|bs|790.|ca|790|cdo|790 nièng|ceb|790|ckb|٧٩٠|crh|790|cs|790|cv|790|cy|790|da|790|de|790|el|790|eml|790|eo|790|es|790|et|790|eu|790|fa|۷۹۰ (میلادی)|fi|790|fo|790|fr|790|fy|790|ga|790|gan|790年|gd|790|gl|790|he|790|hi|790|hr|790.|ht|790 (almanak jilyen)|hu|790|hy|790|id|790|io|790|is|790|it|790|ja|790年|jv|790|ka|790|kk|790 жыл|ko|790년|la|790|lb|790|lij|790|lmo|790|lt|790 m.|lv|790. gads|map_bms|790|mdf|790|mg|790|mhr|790|mk|790|mr|इ.स. ७९०|mrj|790 и|ms|790|mzn|۷۹۰|nah|790|nap|790|nds|790|new|सन् ७९०|nl|790|nn|790|no|790|nrm|790|nso|790|oc|790|or|୭୯୦|os|790-æм аз|pl|790|pnb|790|pt|790|qu|790|ro|790|ru|790 год|rue|790|sa|७९०|scn|790|sd|790ع|sh|790.|shn|790|si|790|sk|790|sl|790|sq|790|sr|790|su|790|sv|790|sw|790|tg|Соли 790|th|พ.ศ. 1333|tk|790|tl|790|tly|790|tr|790|tt|790 ел|uk|790|ur|790ء|uz|790|vec|790|vi|790|war|790|wuu|790年|xmf|790|zh|790年|zh_min_nan|790 nî|zh_yue|790年|qid=Q31147}}) of "{{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ar|شوكو نيهونغي|ca|Shoku Nihongi|cs|Šoku Nihongi|de|Shoku Nihongi|es|Shoku Nihongi|eu|Shoku Nihongi|fa|شوکو نیهونگی|ff|Shoku Nihongi|fr|Shoku Nihongi|id|Shoku Nihongi|it|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本紀|ko|속일본기|ms|Shoku Nihongi|pt|Shoku Nihongi|ru|Сёку нихонги|simple|Shoku Nihongi|sl|Šoku Nihongi|th|โชกุนิฮงงิ|tr|Shoku Nihongi|uk|Сьоку Ніхонґі|zh|續日本紀|qid=Q611399}}". Regarding the Haji clan branch clan in the Sugawara area, the ``Suga family biographies'' also states that the Haji clan resides as ``Since then, the Dobe clan has lived in Sugawara Fushimi Village'' {{Sfn|Sugawara Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}}. In fact, the existence of the Haniwa kiln ruins of the late Sugawara Higashi Ruins (designated historical site by Nara City) from the late {{ill|Kofun period|af|Kofun-tydperk|ar|فترة كوفون|az|Kofun dövrü|be|Кафун|bg|Кофун|bn|কোফুন যুগ|ca|Període Kofun|cs|Období Kofun|de|Kofun-Zeit|eo|Kofun-epoko|es|Período Kofun|eu|Kofun aroa|fa|دوره کوفون|fi|Kofun-kausi|fr|Période Kofun|he|תקופת קופון|hr|Razdoblje Kofun|hu|Kofun-kor|id|Zaman Kofun|it|Periodo Kofun|ja|古墳時代|ko|고훈 시대|lt|Kofun laikotarpis|ms|Zaman Kofun|nl|Kofunperiode|pl|Kofun (okres)|pt|Período Kofun|ro|Perioada Kofun|ru|Период Кофун|sh|Kofunski period|simple|Kofun period|sk|Obdobie Kofun|sl|Obdobje Kofun|sr|Кофун период|sv|Kofunperioden|th|ยุคโคฟุง|tl|Panahong Kofun|tr|Kofun Dönemi|uk|Період Кофун|vi|Thời kỳ Kofun|wuu|古坟时代|zh|古坟时代|zh_min_nan|Kohun sî-tāi|zh_yue|古墳時代|qid=Q459939}} area is known to support the existence of the Haji clan. Sugawara Higashi Ruins Haniwa Kiln Ruins] (Nara City homepage). </ref>It is also noteworthy that the area of ​​worship of Sugawara Shrine almost coincides with the distribution range of the Haji clan. In addition to Sugawara Shrine, history books also include {{ill|Hōraiyama Kofun|ja|宝来山古墳|qid=Q11452574|lt=Sugawara Fushimi Toryo}} ({{ill|Emperor Suinin|ar|الإمبراطور سوينين|arz|الامبراطور سوينين|azb|سوینین (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Suinin|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر سوینین|cs|Suinin|de|Suinin|eo|Suinin|es|Suinin Tennō|fa|امپراتور سوینین|fi|Suinin|fr|Suinin|hr|Suinin|id|Kaisar Suinin|it|Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇|ka|სუინინი|ko|스이닌 천황|lt|Imperatorius Suininas|mn|Эзэн Хаан Сүйнин|nl|Suinin|pl|Suinin|pt|Suinin|ru|Император Суйнин|sh|Car Suinin|simple|Emperor Suinin|sl|Cesar Sujnin|sr|Суинин|sv|Suinin|th|จักรพรรดิซูอินิง|tl|Emperador Suinin|tr|Suinin (imparator)|uk|Імператор Суйнін|uz|Imperator Suinin|vi|Thiên hoàng Suinin|yo|Emperor Suinin|zh|垂仁天皇|zh_min_nan|Suinin Thian-hông|zh_yue|垂仁天皇|qid=Q314850}} tomb) and Sugawara Fushimi West Mausoleum ({{ill|Emperor Ankō|ar|الإمبراطور أنكو|arz|الامبراطور انكو|azb|آنکو (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Ankō|cs|Ankó|de|Ankō|es|Ankō Tennō|fa|امپراتور آنکو|fr|Ankō (empereur)|hr|Ankō|hu|Ankó japán császár|id|Kaisar Ankō|it|Ankō (imperatore del Giappone)|ja|安康天皇|ka|ანკო|ko|안코 천황|nl|Anko (keizer)|pl|Ankō|pt|Anko|ru|Император Анко|sh|Car Ankō|simple|Emperor Ankō|sl|Cesar Anko|sv|Anko|th|จักรพรรดิอังโก|tl|Emperador Ankō|tr|Ankō (imparator)|uk|Імператор Анко|uz|Imperator Ankō|vi|Thiên hoàng Ankō|yo|Emperor Ankō|zh|安康天皇|zh_min_nan|Ankô Thian-hông|zh_yue|安康天皇|qid=Q361010}} tomb).・It is known that the name of Sugawara-dera Temple (currently {{ill|Kikō-ji|de|Kikō-ji|ja|喜光寺|qid=Q11419051}}) is derived from the place name of this area, and the name of the Sugawara clan is also said to be derived from the name of this area {{Sfn|Sugawara clan (ancient clan)|2010}}. The rituals at Sugawara Shrine are thought to have originated when the Haji clan of Sugawara (later known as the Sugawara clan) worshiped their ancestral deity, but in later generations it became the birthplace of Michizane Sugawara. Some theories arose, and it is currently worshiped as a shrine of {{ill|Tenjin faith|ja|天神信仰|ko|천신신앙|qid=Q66890725}} {{Sfn|Sugawara Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1982}}.

== History ==
Founding date is unknown. As mentioned above, it is presumed that the Haji clan (later {{ill|Sugawara clan|de|Sugawara (Klan)|fr|Clan Sugawara|ja|菅原氏|ru|Сугавара (род)|uk|Рід Суґавара|qid=Q1771125}}), whose home base was {{ill|Korean clans|es|Bon-gwan|fr|Système de Pon'gwan|it|Bongwan|ja|本貫|ko|본관|ms|Bon-gwan|pl|Koreańskie klany|ro|Bon-gwan|ru|Пон (корейский клан)|zh|本貫|qid=Q846706}}, worshiped their ancestral deity. Later, when Sugawara-dera Temple ({{ill|Kikō-ji|de|Kikō-ji|ja|喜光寺|qid=Q11419051}}) was built in the southwest, it became its guardian shrine, and it came to be called both Sugawara Shrine and Kikoji Tenmangu Shrine.

== Festival ==
The festivals held annually at Sugawara Tenmangu Shrine are as follows.
* Monthly festival (25th of every month)
* Onda Festival (February 25th)
* Nara Fude Festival (March equinox)
* Birthday Festival, Shinto Ritual (June 25th)
* Regular festival (the day before Sports Day in October)
* Niinamesai (November 25th)

== Related locations ==
[[File:Sugahara-jinja (Nara), Sugahara-in-ato.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Sugawara Tenmangu Ruins Tenjinbori}}]]
* Sugawara Tenmangu Ruins Tenjinbori ({{Coord|34|41|8.16|N|135|46|47.10|E|region:JP-29_type:landmark|name=Sugawara Tenmangu Ruins Tenjinbori}})
: The site of the Sugawara clan's old mansion. In later generations, a theory arose that it was the birthplace of Michizane Sugawara, and the pond is believed to be the birthplace of Michizane. </ref>{{Sfn|Sugawara Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1982}}.
